notes.title: The latest edition of the Scrolls of Sengoku Dynasty is available!
notes.content:
Youkoso!

In today's and for the time being last issue of the Scrolls of Sengoku Dynasty we deal with potables. Let's take a look at what's informative about it.

Nowadays, everyone who has a rudimentary interest in tea is probably familiar with matcha. In the tea ceremony, green tea is served according to strict rules and traditions. Which ones? You can read about them in issue 8.

Do you know what nihonshu is? That's what sake tends to be called in Japan. Sake has about as many percent alcohol as red wine, because it is - unsurprisingly - rice wine. But there is more to know about sake!

Luís Fróis is a name that few people know. A missionary from the Iberian Peninsula, he spent his life in Japan from 1563 and wrote several texts on Japanese culture. What we know about the women of the Japanese Middle Ages we owe to him, among others. You can find out what it is in this issue.

There is also some fan content and other exciting topics in this new issue!

Read up!

notes.title: The newest edition of the Sengoku Scrolls is available!
notes.content:
Youkoso!

Sengoku Dynasty is in Early Access and the scrolls are going into the seventh installment.
What's in it?

For starters, some underworld. Figuratively and literally. Topics include funerals and the associated rites in ancient Japan and the Jizō, the companions of the underworld.

Furthermore, we deal with material that is also important in the game: buildings. Buildings in Japan follow a typical construction method, as you will learn.

Everyone has certainly heard the name Hattori Hanzo, it has often been mentioned in modern pop culture, but what is behind this character? Spoiler: He is not a swordsmith.

These topics and a few more await you in the latest issue of Scrolls of Sengoku.
Have fun reading!

notes.title: The latest edition of the Sengoku Scrolls is now available!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42158774/c6dd489fa737f9774a4ef5335cfedaceff1355e0.png[/img]

Youkoso!

As work continues diligently on the game, let's take a quick look at some of the contents of the latest scrolls.

Ame-no-Uzume is a legendary figure of the Japanese pantheon. She is much discussed among scholars and we try to find a context to a dance. 

An important figure of the late Sengoku and early Edo era is Date Masamune, a warlord and daimyo from northeastern Japan who helped Tokugawa Ieyasu to victory at the Battle of Sekigahara. Read more about this colourful person.

In this issue, we also take a little detour into the Unreal Engine 5 and its new features.

Furthermore, there are interesting facts about paper production, clothing and the scholar Tenjin.

Get this jam-packed new issue of Scrolls of Sengoku Dynasty!

notes.title: The latest issue of the Scrolls of Sengoku Dynasty is out!
notes.content:
Youkoso!

Another copy of the Sengoku Scrolls has made its way over hills and dales to your home sweet home and is ringing your doorbell!

This time in the scroll:

[list]
[*] A brief expert advice for your next visit to the open-air swimming pool in Japan. Bathing properly in the onsen!
[*] Not all ghosts emerge from the television or sit in the attic. Get to know the shikigami and have a pair of scissors and paper ready. You might need both!
[*] Have you heard the name Takeda Shingen before? Read his story in this issue!
[/list]

This and more in issue 4 of the Sengoku Scrolls. Get the Scrolls of Sengoku here!

Have fun with it!

Arigato!
